sections.label: THINKING
sections.content:
SPACE changed the board! Changes:
- ('W','b') 21 pixels, rows 1-61, column 31: the dotted line of the divider disappeared (the white dots at column 31 vanished)!
- ('b','W') 8 pixels, rows 19-28, columns 46-58: 8 white dots appeared on the black piece!
- ('Y','B') 1 pixel, (2,63): the HUD timer decreased.
So SPACE toggled the dots from the divider to the black piece! Looking at the image: the divider is now a plain 3-column band (no dots), and the black piece has white dots on it (2 on the top bar, 2 in the middle, 2 on the bottom bar… 8 dots total).
Interesting! So the dots are a "marker" that can be moved around. In level 1, the dots were on the player piece (the black piece in the left panel). Here, the dots started on the divider, and SPACE moved them to the black piece.
Hmm, wait, actually in level 1 the dots were on the player. Maybe the dots indicate the "active" piece! In level 2, the dots started on the divider (weird), and SPACE moved them to the black piece.
So maybe SPACE cycles the "active" piece: divider → black → charcoal → …? If the dots are on the black piece, then arrow keys control the black piece!
This changes everything: maybe the goal is to move the black piece (now active) to a specific location. The black piece is a Z-shape at rows 18-29, columns 45-59.
Hmm, but what's the target for the black piece? The yellow is an S-shape in the left panel. The black is a Z-shape. They're not the same shape.
Wait, maybe the dots indicate which piece is the "player," and the goal is for the player's mirror image to cover the yellow. If the black is active: its mirror image across the divider (center 31) is: top bar 45-53 → 2*31−53=9 to 2*31−45=17 → columns 9-17, rows 18-20; middle 51-53 → 9-11, rows 21-26; bottom 51-59 → 3-11, rows 27-29. That's exactly the charcoal's position! Of course — the charcoal is the black's mirror image.
So the two pieces are always mirror images of each other across the divider. The dots mark the active piece. SPACE toggles which piece is active (or cycles it).
Goal hypothesis: move the active piece so that its mirror image covers the yellow. If the black (Z) is active, its mirror image is the S-shape at the charcoal's position — but the charcoal's position is fixed by the black's position… no wait, if the black is active and moves, the charcoal (its mirror image) moves too. The yellow is at rows 42-53. The mirror image of the black is at the same rows as the black (18-29). The yellow is at rows 42-53. The rows will never match (the mirror image across a vertical axis preserves rows).
So the goal can't be for the mirror image to cover the yellow… unless the divider can move vertically? The divider is vertical; if the divider moves horizontally, the mirror image's columns change but the rows stay the same.
Hmm, so how could any piece ever cover the yellow (rows 42-53)? Only if the piece itself moves vertically. But vertical movement was blocked…
Wait, maybe vertical movement was blocked because the active piece was the charcoal, and… no, that's not it. Hmm.
Let me reconsider: maybe the dots on the divider meant "the divider is active," and SPACE moved the dots to the black piece to make it active. Now that the black is active, maybe arrow keys can move the black piece — including vertically? Let me test: with the black active, try DOWN.
No, wait. Let me reconsider the whole thing. Maybe the goal is: get the dots (the marker) onto the yellow piece? The dots are now on the black. Maybe SPACE cycles the dots: divider → black → charcoal → yellow → …? If SPACE moves the dots to the next piece, then pressing SPACE a few more times might put the dots on the yellow, and that could be the goal (marking the target)? That seems too trivial.
Or maybe the dots indicate which piece you can move, and the goal is to move the pieces so that the active piece's mirror image covers the yellow… but the rows don't match.
Hmm, wait. Let me re-verify: is the yellow really at rows 42-53? Let me re-measure the yellow. And also re-verify that the charcoal and black are exact mirror images.
Actually, let me test whether the black piece can now be moved with arrow keys (now that it's active). Try RIGHT and DOWN on the black.

sections.label: ASSISTANT
sections.content: SPACE moved the white dots from the divider onto the black piece — the dots mark the *active* piece. Now testing whether arrow keys control the black piece (and whether vertical movement works for it).

sections.label: TOOL CALL: python
sections.content:
<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>

r = action(['DOWN'])
print("DOWN:", r.get('board_changed'))
lines = current_frame.ascii.split('\n')
def ext(ch, c0, c1):
    ps=[(i,j) for i in range(64) for j in range(c0,c1) if lines[i][j]==ch]
    if not ps: return None
    rs=[p[0] for p in ps]; cs=[p[1] for p in ps]
    return (min(rs),max(rs),min(cs),max(cs))
print("black:", ext('B',36,63))
print("charcoal:", ext('c',0,30))
if r.get('board_changed'):
    from collections import defaultdict
    before = previous_frame.ascii.split('\n')
    g=defaultdict(list)
    for i in range(len(before)):
        for j in range(len(before[i])):
            if before[i][j]!=lines[i][j]: g[(before[i][j],lines[i][j])].append((i,j))
    for k,v in g.items():
        rs=[p[0] for p in v]; cs=[p[1] for p in v]
        print(k,len(v),"rows",min(rs),max(rs),"cols",min(cs),max(cs))
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
